$2{X}^{2}(1 - \cos \theta ) = {n}^{2} \cdot 2{X}^{2}(1 + \cos \theta ) 1 - \cos \theta = {n}^{2} + {n}^{2}\cos \theta \cos \theta = \frac{1 - {n}^{2}}{1 + {n}^{2}} \theta = {\cos }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{{n}^{2} - 1}{ - {n}^{2} - 1}\right)$

questions.question: Two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ have equal magnitudes. The magnitude of $\left(\vec{A} + \vec{B}\right)$ is ' $n$ ' times the magnitude of $\left(\vec{A} - \vec{B}\right)$ . The angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is:
questions.explanation:
Given: $\left(\vec{A} + \vec{B}\right) = n\left(\vec{A} - \vec{B}\right)$, so, the magnitudes of this will be given as,

$\sqrt{{A}^{2} + {B}^{2} + 2ABcos\theta } = n\left(\sqrt{{A}^{2} + {B}^{2} - 2ABcos\theta }\right)$;where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$.

Also, $\left(\vec{A}\right) = \left(\vec{B}\right)$,

$\sqrt{2{A}^{2} + 2{A}^{2}cos\theta } = n\sqrt{2{A}^{2} - 2{A}^{2}cos\theta }$

Squaring both sides:

$2{A}^{2}\left(1 + cos\theta \right) = {n}^{2}2{A}^{2}\left(1 - cos\theta \right) cos\theta = \frac{{n}^{2} - 1}{{n}^{2} + 1}$

i.e., $\theta = {cos}^{ - 1}\left(\frac{{n}^{2} - 1}{{n}^{2} + 1}\right)$

questions.question: A body of mass $(5 \pm 0.5)\mathrm{kg}$ is moving with a velocity of $(20 \pm 0.4)m{s}^{ - 1}.$ Its kinetic energy will be
questions.explanation:
The kinetic energy is given by,

$K = \frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Differentiating the above equation,

$dK = \frac{1}{2}({v}^{2}dm + 2mvdv)$

Dividing by $K$,

$\implies \frac{dK}{K} = \frac{dm}{m} + \frac{2dv}{v} \implies \frac{dK}{1000} = \frac{0.5}{5} + \frac{2 \times 0.4}{20} \implies dK = 100 + 40 = 140 \implies KE = (1000 \pm 140)J$

Relation of the relative errors will be,

questions.question: Two resistance are given as ${R}_{1} = (10 \pm 0.5)\Omega$ and ${R}_{2} = (15 \pm 0.5)\Omega .$ The percentage error in the measurement of equivalent resistance when they are connected in parallel is
questions.explanation:
For a parallel combination the equivalent resistance is

$\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{{R}_{1}} + \frac{1}{{R}_{2}}...(i)$

A general expression for error can be written as $x \pm \Delta x$

Differentiating equation (i)

$\frac{dR}{{R}^{2}} = \frac{d{R}_{1}}{{R}_{1}^{2}} + \frac{d{R}_{2}}{{R}_{2}^{2}}...(ii)$

The equivalent resistance with ${R}_{1} = 10\Omega & {R}_{2} = 15\Omega$ is

$\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} \implies R = \frac{150}{25} = 6\Omega$

Substituting the above value in equation (ii)

$dR = 36\left(\frac{0.5}{100} + \frac{0.5}{15 \times 15}\right) = 0.26 \implies R = 6 \pm 0.26$

Hence, the percentage error is

$\frac{dR}{R} \times 100 = \frac{0.26}{6} \times 100 = 4.33%$
